featured_reviews.name: Carl Rebello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Been meaning to visit this place for what seemed like forever but the wait times always make me decide to walk away. This time we decided to wait since the wait for a table was just 10-15 minutes.

We were seated in the third cafe but since we didn't like the atmosphere we asked if we could sit in the main cafe, the staff were pleasant and said it wasn't a problem we just needed to wait a few more minutes while they free up a table.

We got our table and were seated on the top section, the seating is unique and if you're tall please mind your head 😅.

We ordered just coffee this time but to be fair one of the coffees was more dessert than coffee (I'm not complaining). So the coconut cold brew which I got wasn't particularly my favourite, I honestly didn't care much for the combination of coconut and coffee but my wife did enjoy it.

The other "drink" that we got was the Iced EDCM which also the coffee part I didn't care for much and neither did my wife but what was amazing was the mousse, that chocolate mousse was delicious and just should be enjoyed on it own.

One thing I didn't like though was in most of the coffee options there's a statement made in the description "choice of milk" which would normally mean you get to choose the milk of your choice as it's included in the price but it isn't. On the top of the menu it gives you a list of milk options and a price but I naturally assumed this would be the case if you chose to swap the milk of your given drink to another but no it applies to all drinks including the ones that ask for your choice of milk. The wording should be made clear or the servers should relay this message to the guests even if it's not a huge amount. In fact a table next to us also didn't expect the charge on their bill as they weren't aware.

Really nice place. Great location, proper Bandra vibe, and solid food.

I am a nachos person, but let’s be honest, most places mess them up. Only a few actually get it right, and Boone is one of them. The nachos were god-level good. Like order-again-even-if-you’re-full good.

The space is beautifully put together. Very boujee but still comfortable, not trying too hard. Overall, a great café in Bandra with the right mix of vibe, food, and energy. Would definitely go back.

featured_reviews.name: Ninad joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to this spot on Saturday morning for breakfast, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience for us.

We ordered one Cortado, a large Pain au Chocolat, a spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown, an avocado chicken sandwich, and a Caramel Latte.

The cortado was incredible; it's a traditional Spanish espresso drink made with double espresso and 60 ml of milk. It had a bitter flavour, but I really enjoyed it.

The large pain au chocolat was absolutely delicious, a classic pastry crafted from buttery, flaky, laminated dough (similar to croissant dough) wrapped around dark chocolate sticks.

The spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown was tasty, featuring shredded potatoes filled with cooked chicken, pan-fried until golden and crispy.The avocado chicken sandwich was mouthwatering and highly recommended. It was a fresh, nutritious, and versatile meal made with thin slices of chicken and avocado. Simply delightful.

The caramel latte was incredibly refreshing. It’s a sweet and creamy coffee drink typically made with espresso, steamed milk, and caramel syrup.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great experience at Boojee Cafe. Absolutely loved how this cafe is designed-it may look small from the outside, but the interiors are planned so well that it feels surprisingly spacious and comfortable once you step in. It’s a perfect spot for a quick bite with friends or even a casual catch-up over coffee.

The place gets quite packed on weekends. We went on a Saturday and had to wait around 5–10 minutes for a table, which honestly just shows how popular the cafe is.

The food and coffee here are fantastic. The House Cold Coffee was suggested to us and it truly lived up to the hype, a must-try if you’re a genuine coffee lover. We also tried the Orange Cold Brew. Personally, I didn’t enjoy it as much, but it definitely feels like an acquired taste, so cold brew enthusiasts should still give it a shot.

For food, we tried the Chicken & Veggies Mini Wrap and it was amazing, especially the dip served alongside it which paired perfectly with the wrap.

Another big plus point was the staff and service. The staff is friendly, welcoming and the service is impressively quick despite the crowd.

Overall, a really nice cafe with great vibes, good food and excellent coffee. Would definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in and around Bandra.

review_photos.caption: Chicken Wrap and Orange Cold Brew

featured_reviews.name: Kamlesh Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Boojee Cafe in Bandra West, Mumbai, has received rave reviews from visitors. Here's what they're saying
- *Ambiance*: The cafe has a cozy, quaint atmosphere with a beautiful combination of simple black and white decor. It's perfect for relaxed conversations, meetings or just unwinding with a good cup of coffee.
- *Food*: The menu offers a range of options, including Greek salads, espresso dark chocolate mousse, ABC apple beetroot carrot juice and mushroom bruschetta. Visitors have praised the food, saying it's "awesome" and "delicious".
- *Service*: The staff is extremely friendly, cute and knowledgeable about the menu. They provide quick service, making it a great spot for busy professionals or groups.
- *Value for Money*: While some visitors felt the prices were a bit steep, others believed the quality and experience justified the cost. The average price range is around ₹500-₹1,000 for two people.

*Some notable mentions*:
- *Greek Salad*: Fresh cucumbers, salad leaves, feta cheese, black olives, cherry tomatoes and a lovely dressing.
- *Espresso Dark Chocolate Mousse*: Light, melt-in-your-mouth texture and rich flavor.
- *ABC Apple Beetroot Carrot Juice*: Refreshing and perfect for health-conscious visitors.

*Overall Experience*: Boojee Cafe has a 4.4-star rating on Restaurant Guru and 4.5-star rating on Tripadvisor, with visitors praising its great ambiance, delicious food and excellent service

featured_reviews.name: Chirag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved our visit to Boojee Cafe in Mumbai! The eggs benedict with salmon were spot on, and the Turkish eggs were also great —rich, flavourful, and perfectly balanced. The pistachio croissant was heavenly.

Such a refreshing find in India—this place genuinely feels like an Australasian-style café, from the quality of the food to the overall vibe. Great coffee, great menu, and a really relaxed atmosphere. Highly recommend if you’re after a proper brunch experience!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had brunch here for the first time after hearing about it from colleagues. I ordered the Truffle cheddar scrambled eggs and a black tea .
The scrambled eggs were delicious and served with a salad and sourdough bread . Excellent combination. The tea was Twinings so a clear focus on quality.
Here is where I was disappointed ..the music at first was way too loud to finish my work, let alone think but a lady called Jhanvi very sweetly noticed and lowered the volume.
Also in attendance were a couple of flies (unnecessary desi touch ) and my eggs were served in a chipped plate.

However, on the positive side, Ebrahim and Imam were warm and friendly , served my food , asked how it tasted  and kindly returned my sunglasses I left behind . It didn’t feel forced .

Afterwards I spoke to Jhanvi ,the sweet smiley lady who rescued me from going deaf and turns out she is in charge of Marketing. She was most responsive to my feedback .

I wish this beautiful located Cafe the best of luck and hope they do well enough to lower the prices a tad . For my eggs and tea I paid Rs 736, of which Rs 96 was service charge + taxes. Left a rather small cash tip as I paid a 10% service charge .

Speaking of which , they lost electricity just when it came to swiping my credit card so I paid in cash.
All in all a cute pricey place with a menu that’s trendy .
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Nalini,
It's wonderful to hear you enjoyed the Truffle cheddar scrambled eggs and appreciated the quality of the Twinings tea. Your feedback about the music and the flies is invaluable, and I’m glad Jhanvi could assist in creating a more comfortable environment for you. We’re addressing the issue with the chipped plate to ensure the presentation of our dishes matches their quality. Thank you for your kind wishes; we’ll continue working to enhance your experience.
Thank you,
Team Grounded

name: Love in Langos
description:
Langos is a typical Hungarian food. Nowadays it is a deep fried flatbread, but in the past it was made of the last bits of the bread-dough and baked at the front of a brick or clay oven, to be served hot as the breakfast of the bread-baking day.
Up to the mid 20th century, bread was baked once a week due to the cost of heating up the large oven and the lengthy proces. Because the bread loaf, typical to Hungary, was 6 to 10 pounds each, traditionally they used to bake smaller (1-2 pounds) "cipó" rolls for the evening and the next day. The name lángos (literally meaning "flamed") comes from baking these flat breads.

Love in Lagos - Cafe serves both baked and Fried versions. Lets try some.

The café is listed as opening at 7:30 AM, and I’ve stopped by a few times around then after morning workouts. However, each time, the team has still been in the middle of setting up—cleaning, switching on machines—and not ready to serve even a simple coffee. If 7:30 AM is the stated opening time, it would be reasonable to expect at least basic service from then. Otherwise, it may be more accurate to list the opening time as 8:00 AM.

More importantly, on a couple of occasions, the person managing the morning shift (appears to be a lady dressed in black in a supervisory role) has responded in a rather abrupt and not very welcoming manner—almost as if customers are interrupting the opening process. It came across as dismissive, and at times borderline rude. This is what prompted me to finally write this.

I enjoy the space and have otherwise had good experiences here, which is why I hope this feedback is taken constructively. A more prepared and welcoming start to the day would make a big difference, especially given the number of early-morning visitors in the neighbourhood.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very ghastly and amusing experience at the Village Shop. I spent a Monday morning here, was hoping to get my coffee and breakfast  in some peace and quiet. It was only me in the cafe and the owner with 2 of her staff on another table.
In the first 10 mins I figured the owner had issues with staff, even though they spoke in hushed tones.

I let it slide. Naturally, I have no context of that conversation.
The food wasn’t up to the mark. They had it replaced without getting defensive.

Then, after a few mins I spoke loudly because I was on a call, and there was no one else in the cafe but me and the owner, I was asked to speak softly. She was irked. I gladly obliged.

I stepped outside to take my call. For 45 mins. In the heat. You see, I have been brought up with a lot of empathy.
It felt like my grandmother gave me a punishment to not enter the house.

What a ghastly experience for a Bandra cafe.  I hope the owners have the business acumen to start something else of their own. Customer centricity and empathy are not the strongest suit of some of the most affluent people in Bandra. What tarnishes reputation is lack of empathy for staff and no understanding of what customer focus looks like.

Money can’t buy you manners or class.

Its evident to me today, yet again :)

🍜 Japanese Ramen Bowl (₹520) – The quantity was generous, and the flavours were quite nice. It’s a comforting bowl and filling enough for one person.
🍳 Shakshouka (₹400) – This one was surprisingly good! The taste was on point, and the portion size was enough for two people to share.
🥤 Blueberry Spirulina Smoothie (₹400) – Sadly, this was the only miss for us. It mostly tasted like banana with barely any blueberry flavour, so it didn’t feel worth the price.

The service was quite slow — it took about 35–40 minutes for our food to arrive, even though the café wasn’t crowded when we visited.

Overall, I’d give 3/5 stars. The pricing is definitely on the higher side, and while the food was decent, it’s not something I’d crave to go back for (except maybe to try their smoothie bowls next time!).

featured_reviews.review_text: This tiny cafe on Waterfield Road is perfect for dinner with you and your family. The cozy setting, featuring pale green and pink decorations, gives you that perfect peaceful atmosphere. Earth Cafe offers a variety of options whether you’re vegetarian, Jain or just wanting something different. The food is high quality with something for everyone. The avocado bruschetta has the perfect amount of crispness and flavour. The fries are freshly made, perfect for a crunchy starter. The peach and mint mojito is to die for. To choose a main dish is nearly impossible. From freshly baked sourdough pizzas or piping hot risotto. The lasagna is an amazing dish with layered zucchini and a creamy vegan sauce. featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Monat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Candies, Bandra West – A Festive Wonderland with Timeless Charm

Candies in Bandra West is not just a restaurant, it’s an experience — especially during Christmas and New Year. The moment you step inside, it feels like you’ve walked into a cozy European festive village. Every corner is thoughtfully decorated with twinkling fairy lights, Christmas trees, wreaths, bells, stars, ribbons, and warm glowing lamps that instantly lift your mood. The décor doesn’t feel artificial or overdone — it feels personal, handcrafted, and full of warmth.

What truly stands out is how creatively the space is used. The unique seating style makes Candies feel more like a series of small artistic zones rather than one big café. There are intimate nooks, balcony-style seating, stair-side tables, wooden benches, cozy corners, and open-air sections, each decorated differently. No two seating areas feel the same, which makes every visit special and photo-worthy.

During Christmas and New Year, the place transforms even more beautifully with festive lighting and seasonal decorations, creating a warm, nostalgic, and celebratory atmosphere. Whether you’re seated indoors surrounded by décor or outside enjoying the Bandra breeze, the ambience feels magical.

The food matches the charm of the place. Candies offers a good mix of both veg and non-veg options, making it suitable for everyone. Their desserts are especially worth trying — fresh, comforting, and perfect to end the meal on a sweet note.
Candies perfectly blends creative décor, comfortable seating, and satisfying food, making it an ideal spot for friends, couples, families, or even solo visits. If you love places with character, soul, and festive charm, Candies during the holiday season is a must-visit.

✨ A place where décor tells a story and every seat feels special. ✨

Visited Veronica on a Saturday evening around 8 PM. There was about a 30-minute wait, but I really appreciated the fairness and transparency of their queue system—it was easy to generate a token and track our place in line.

Unfortunately, the much-talked-about chicken burger was already sold out by the time we ordered, which was a bit disappointing. That said, the staff more than made up for it with their warm and attentive service, especially towards our child.

We ordered the Cheese Melt, Chicken Shawarma, and a Bagel that had a unique twist which I absolutely loved. To drink, we had the Vietnamese Coffee and Cold Brew, both of which were excellent. For our kid, we got the French Fries and Almond Croissant. They were fairly average but perfectly fine for children.

What really stood out was the hospitality. The staff were wonderful with kids and even brought a complimentary hot chocolate-style drink for our child, which was a lovely gesture on top of the already excellent service.

Overall, a great experience with good food, excellent coffee, and genuinely warm service. The well-managed queue system and family-friendly atmosphere made the visit even better. I'd definitely come back—hopefully early enough to try the chicken burger next time.

Bombay Salad Co., Bandra – Healthy, Hearty & Actually Delicious 🥗☕

Sip • Grab • Taste

Visited Bombay Salad Co. on a Saturday with family, and this place genuinely delivers on the healthy-but-still-tasty promise. The menu is built for health-conscious eaters, but even someone who isn’t into salads will find plenty to enjoy here.

📍 Location & Access
It’s located just off Linking Road, but the approach lane is quite narrow. Valet parking is not available, so if you’re driving, it’s smarter to park a little ahead and walk. Avoid taking the car right to the door not worth the stress.

🍴 What We Ordered:

Three Salad Bowls – we chose the small bowls, but the portions were still surprisingly generous. Fresh greens, good balance of protein and crunch, and well-made dressings nothing watery or bland here.

Cappuccino – smooth, well-made, not bitter. A nice warm pairing with fresh salads.

✨ Ambience & Experience
The vibe is calm, cozy, and “feel good” without trying too hard. Staff is polite, service is steady, and the ingredients felt fresh  which is the real win for a salad-focused place.

⭐ Overall Verdict:
If you're looking for healthy food that doesn't taste like a compromise, Bombay Salad Co. hits the mark.
Great for a relaxed meal, post-gym brunch, or a weekend family catch-up.

Another one for the foodie trail – SGT Reviews ✍️
